leads.title: Mexico City Civil Code Amendments - Transgender birth certificate changes
leads.documents: Allows transgender people to change gender and name on birth certificates in Mexico City.
leads.detail: Cited in timeline as took effect 13 March 2004

leads.title: Mexico City Legislative Assembly law on transgender gender change
leads.documents: Makes it easier for transgender people to change gender on birth certificates.
leads.detail: Cited as passed September 2008 by Mexico City Legislative Assembly

leads.title: Legislative Assembly of Mexico City gender identity law
leads.documents: Makes process for transgender people to change gender much quicker and simpler.

leads.title: Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation ruling on transgender birth certificate modification
leads.documents: Holds person can change name and gender marker through simple administrative process based solely on self-declaration of gender identity; described as first of its kind.

leads.title: Inter-American Court of Human Rights ruling on same-sex marriage and gender identity
leads.documents: Rules same-sex marriage and recognition of gender identity on official documents are human rights protected by American Convention on Human Rights; Mexico is signatory.

leads.title: Article 1, Constitution of Mexico amendment prohibiting discrimination
leads.documents: Prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation; inserts precise term 'sexual orientation' into federal constitutional protection.
leads.detail: Cited as amended 2001 with term 'preferences', then June 2011 with 'sexual orientation'

leads.title: Federal anti-discrimination law and national council
leads.documents: Creates federal prohibition on discrimination and creates national council to enforce it.
leads.detail: Cited as passed 29 April 2003, took effect 11 June 2003

leads.title: Mexico City ordinance banning discrimination based on sexual orientation
leads.documents: First ordinance of its kind in Mexico banning discrimination based on sexual orientation.
leads.detail: Cited as passed 2 September 1999 by PRD-controlled Legislative Assembly of the Federal District

leads.title: Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation jurisprudential thesis on marriage
leads.documents: Expands legal definition of marriage to encompass same-sex couples; laws restricting marriage to man and woman deemed unconstitutional and discriminatory, binding all justice providers.
leads.detail: Cited as released 3 June 2015; also referenced as 14 June 2015 declaration

leads.title: Supreme Court nationwide jurisprudence on same-sex adoption / parental rights
leads.documents: Binds all lower court judges to rule in favor of same-sex couples seeking adoption and parental rights; follows Campeche adoption ban case.
leads.detail: Cited as finalized 23 September 2016; related rulings 11 August 2015 and September 2016
